scheme_name: Scheme for Relief to the Un-registered Workers
description:
The Scheme for Relief to the Un-registered Workers was launched by the Government of India on 26th October 2020. 

This scheme was introduced in response to the challenges faced by unregistered workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to unregistered workers who were severely impacted by the economic downturn caused by the pandemic. 

The scheme aims to support the livelihood of these workers by offering them a one-time financial relief of ₹3,000. 

This amount is intended to help cover essential expenses such as food, housing, and healthcare. 

The scheme specifically targets unregistered workers in the informal sector, who often lack access to social security benefits. 

According to estimates, there are approximately 42 crore unregistered workers in India. 

These workers include daily wage laborers, construction workers, domestic workers, and agricultural laborers. 

The scheme was designed to reach out to these vulnerable groups effectively. 

To be eligible for the benefits under this scheme, applicants must meet specific criteria. 

The applicant must be an unregistered worker in the informal sector. 

The age of the applicant must be at least 18 years. 

There is no upper age limit specified for eligibility. 

The applicant must not be a member of any registered trade union. 

The income of the applicant should not exceed ₹10,000 per month. 

This income criterion ensures that the assistance reaches those who are genuinely in need. 

The application process for the Scheme for Relief to the Un-registered Workers is straightforward. 

Interested applicants must visit the official website of the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

The application form is available for download on the website. 

Applicants are required to fill out the form with accurate details. 

The completed application form must be submitted along with necessary documents. 

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Additionally, applicants must provide proof of their unregistered worker status. 

This can be done through self-declaration or by providing relevant documents from employers. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The timeline for processing applications is typically within 30 days from the date of submission. 

Successful applicants will receive the financial assistance directly into their bank accounts. 

The disbursement of funds is done through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system. 

This ensures that the funds reach the beneficiaries without any intermediaries. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

The ministry has set up a dedicated helpline for queries related to the scheme. 

The contact number for the helpline is 1800 425 1515. 

The scheme has been well-received by the target population. 

As of September 2023, over 1.5 crore applications have been received under the scheme. 

Out of these, approximately 1.2 crore applications have been approved. 

The total amount disbursed under the scheme has exceeded ₹36,000 crore. 

This financial support has played a crucial role in alleviating the hardships faced by unregistered workers. 

The scheme also aims to create awareness about the rights of unregistered workers. 

It encourages them to seek registration and access social security benefits in the future. 

The government has partnered with various NGOs and civil society organizations to promote the scheme. 

These organizations help in reaching out to unregistered workers in remote areas. 

They assist in the application process and provide guidance on eligibility criteria. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Indian government to enhance social security for unorganized workers. 

It aligns with the objectives of the Social Security Code 2020, which aims to provide comprehensive social security benefits to all workers. 

The government has committed to continuously monitoring the implementation of the scheme. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate its effectiveness and reach. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme further. 

The scheme is expected to evolve based on the changing needs of unregistered workers. 

Future enhancements may include increasing the financial assistance amount or expanding eligibility criteria. 

The government is also exploring the possibility of providing additional benefits such as skill development programs. 

These programs would aim to empower unregistered workers with skills for better employment opportunities. 

The Scheme for Relief to the Un-registered Workers is a significant step towards ensuring social security for vulnerable populations. 

It reflects the government's commitment to supporting the informal sector during crises. 

The scheme's success is crucial for the economic recovery of the country post-pandemic. 

It aims to build a more resilient workforce that can withstand future challenges. 

The scheme is expected to continue until the economic situation stabilizes. 

The government has allocated a substantial budget for the ongoing support of unregistered workers. 

This initiative is a testament to the government's recognition of the contributions made by unregistered workers to the economy. 

In conclusion, the Scheme for Relief to the Un-registered Workers is a vital welfare initiative. 

It provides immediate financial relief to those most affected by the pandemic. 

The scheme's structured approach ensures that assistance reaches the intended beneficiaries efficiently. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to uplift the livelihoods of unregistered workers across India. 

This initiative is just one of many efforts to strengthen the social safety net for all workers in the country.
